newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania hopes for Rwandan refugee flood home.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania hopes for Rwandan refugee flood home.

text.p: Large numbers of Hutu refugees are expected to return to Rwanda from Tanzania on Saturday after troops stopped them escaping into the bush, aid workers said.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said Tanzanian authorities ruled on Friday Rwandan refugees would no longer be allowed to remain in their camps in northwestern Tanzania.
Aid workers expected refugees from Benaco, 17 km (10 miles) from the Rwandan border, and in its satellite camp Musuhura Hill, to be shepherded back to Rwanda by police and troops on Saturday.
Thousands of heavily-armed troops surrounded Benaco camp, the largest in Tanzania, after large numbers of refugees rushed past stick-wielding soldiers back to the camp they fled only hours earlier.
Hundreds of thousands of refugees slept on the road back to the camps and Rwandan border under army guard, having failed in their bid to flee into the bush since last Sunday.

"The operation is now completely in the hands of the Tanzanian military," said UNHCR official Anne Willem Bijleveld who believed refugees would soon be ordered by the Tanzanian authorities to return to Rwanda, which they fled in 1994.
The UNHCR oposes the forced repatriation of the nearly 540,000 Rwandan refugees in Tanzania.

It was unclear what will happen to Hutu hardline militiamen and troops refusing to go back because they face jail for their part in the slaughter of up to 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in 1994. There are also 112,000 Burundian refugees in Tanzania.
Soldiers beat some refugees at Benaco with sticks on Friday but gave up when it was clear they could not keep them from returning to the camp.
At one point troops fired tear gas canisters and shot in the air to keep the refugees on the road back towards the border.

UNHCR said 1,463 refugees voluntarily returned on Friday, bringing the total number to go back to 7,224 since a Tanzanian government deadline of December 31 was set last week for all 542,000 Rwandan refugees in northwestern Tanzania to go home.
Refugees started leaving the camps last Sunday, saying they were on a marathon trek to asylum in Kenya or as far south as Malawi, 850 km (530 miles) away, to avoid being forced home.
"Go back to the camps and you will get fed. We don't want you here. We want you to go back," Tanzanian army Colonel Urbano Nguvumali told refugees as they were stopped from fleeing into the bush.

The exodus had threatened a repeat of events in Zaire in November when over half-a-million Rwandan Hutus escaping a revolt by Zairean rebels left camps to return to Rwanda or fled or were driven by Hutu militia deeper into Zaire.
Tanzania and UNHCR announced the refugees should go home by the end of this month in the hope of a mass return because of the momentum generated by the relatively smooth move from Zaire.
But the human rights group Amnesty International and a Hutu refugee lobby group said it amounted to forced repatriation.
